item.title: Melody For a Tortured Soul:
item.content:encoded:
Here's my review from the Art Exchange forum:

This is a story whose emotional impact was aided by my having Spirited Away's end credits song playing in the background while I read… but nonetheless, it's about a guy learning a better way to cope. Pretty short, didn't hit as hard as it could have (I had not much reason to get attached to this character), and a bit on the nose at the end, but not bad in any respects. Good incorporation of SCP-4562, as well.

Nothing much has changed, except that the CSS is now sexy.

item.title: Dire Wolf: Re: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Sorry, sorry, I just remembered the initials GM and thought "George? George sounds right."

Alright, so, I have a bit more to spill here. I was gonna do it in an edit to the author post but… nah. So, you may remember that I got you for a previous Art Exchange as well. I wasn't going to gift to you again except Elogee FishTruck and each did one half of the gifter/giftee organization and he forgot that I'd gifted to you so recently. Not a dig at him at all, just not something I would have done, and it was too close to giving people the PMs as to who they were gifting to change things around, so it went through.

But I see it as an opportunity, because there's some stuff I'd like to say, to my writing acquaintance Conwell. When last I gave you a present, it was rather self-serving, as it was 10,000 words of establishing my own GoI, WWS, in the Those Twisted Pines canon. While I do think you liked On the Radar, it launched into some rather unfortunate, and I believe kind of selfish moves on my part. See, I thought that putting WWS in your canon would have been cool and collaborative. And it would have been!

If you liked it.

And, as it turned out, you ended up rather lukewarm on the WWS tale series that I was setting in the Pacific Northwest. The 16 tales I tagged with your canon, the Stories My Dad Told Me tales, were barely relevant to anything in the canon, except that near the end the intersection with Site-64 and connection to On the Radar became clear. And now, they take up a very eyecatching amount of space on your canon's hub.

An amount of space that makes me the second-largest Twisted Pines contributor in terms of article count, and yet I had barely read any of it when I started writing for it. That has been largely remedied now, as I read the majority of the Anderson Robotics arc via researching for this gift, which I kind of see as "making it up to you". And, using this as a way to open the door for conversation… would you rather I remove the twisted-pines tag from the first third of the WWS series and remove them from your hub? If you don't think they're adding anything, which is a possibility I have been quietly expecting for a while, I think it'd be best if I simply removed them. And then this, which more directly ties into everything you've so worked to create, can replace it, and I can be an actual contributor to your canon, not just on a technicality but in spirit.

item.title: SCP-005: Re: Quick Question
item.content:encoded:
How is this sentient?

From the article:

In approximately 50% of cases where a volunteer was not able to identify a locking device as such, SCP-005 was not successful in deactivating the device. Due to these results, SCP-005 has been tentatively classified as 'sentient' and further tests are being run to determine its cognitive abilities.

item.title: Home is where I want to be: Happy Holidays, Zyn!
item.content:encoded:
Home, is where I want to be
But I guess I'm already there
I come home, she lifted up her wings
I guess that this must be the place


~David Byrne, "This Must Be the Place"

This tale is my attempt at emulating the style of Zyn's original Kiryu Labs series — probably one of the best early series on this site, propped up by Zyn's talent for writing heartwarming, touching stories with just the right balance between humour and heartfelt emotion. I hope I did Kiryu Labs justice with this.

Thanks to VoidLady, not_a_seagull, and Its a Bad Idea for helping me revise and edit this tale, and special thanks to Zyn for all that she does to help this community thrive. Have a wonderful New Year.

item.title: A Josie Holiday:
item.content:encoded:
This is a perfect gift for someone who loves Josie the Half Cat, and also asked about hot chocolate being featured in their tale they got. It's simple, it's cute, it meets all the giftee's wishes, who could ask for more? Josie content, anomalous eggnog, cats batting at ornaments. Merry Christmas.

That was my review on the Art Exchange forum, and I don't think my opinion has changed much. It's a simple story, it's a cute story, it's a worthy Art Exchange gift. +1
